cassava.description: Cassava is a drought-tolerant root crop widely grown in tropical regions. It is rich in carbohydrates and serves as a staple food for millions.
cassava.fertilization: Apply balanced NPK fertilizer every 4-6 weeks.
cassava.pest_control: Monitor for cassava mealybugs and root rot.
cassava.uses: Used for flour, animal feed, and biofuel.

growth_stages.description: Cuttings are placed in well-drained soil.

cassava.harvesting: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and fall.

tomato.description: Tomato is a popular fruiting crop grown worldwide. It is rich in vitamins A and C and can be eaten raw or cooked.
tomato.pest_control: Watch for whiteflies and tomato blight.
tomato.uses: Used for fresh consumption, sauces, and soups.

growth_stages.description: Seeds sown in nursery or direct.
Green fruits develop and turn red.
Full red color indicates harvest ready.

tomato.harvesting: Pick when firm and fully colored.

potato.description: Potato is a widely grown root vegetable cultivated for its starchy tubers. It is a staple food in many countries.
potato.watering: Keep soil moist but not waterlogged.
potato.fertilization: Apply potassium-rich fertilizer as tubers develop.
potato.uses: Commonly boiled, baked, fried, or mashed.

growth_stages.description: Tubers begin to swell at stolon ends.

potato.harvesting: Harvest after vines have naturally died.

ube.description: Ube, or purple yam, is a starchy root crop known for its vibrant purple flesh and sweet flavor.
ube.pest_control: Monitor for yam beetles and mealybugs.
ube.uses: Used in Filipino desserts and ice cream.
ube.harvesting: Harvest when vines turn brown and dry.

kamote.description: Kamote, or sweet potato, is a hardy root crop cultivated for its sweet tubers and edible leaves.
kamote.uses: Tubers and young shoots are both edible.

growth_stages.description: Roots start to thicken into tubers.

onion.description: Onion is a widely cultivated bulb vegetable known for its pungent flavor and layers. It is a fundamental ingredient in cuisines worldwide.
onion.watering: Water regularly, especially during bulb formation; reduce watering as they mature.
onion.fertilization: Apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer during early growth.
onion.pest_control: Watch for onion flies, thrips, and downy mildew.
onion.uses: Used as a base for many dishes, can be eaten raw, cooked, or pickled.

growth_stages.description: Seeds, sets, or transplants are placed in fertile soil.
Green shoots emerge from the soil.
Foliage grows to provide energy for the bulb.
Base of the plant starts to swell into a bulb.
Leaves fall over and turn brown.

onion.harvesting: Harvest when tops turn yellow and fall over.
